# PhysicsConstraintMotor <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Physics](Blitz3D-Physics)

</div>


```blitzbasic
PhysicsConstraintMotor:Void constraint:Int32, mode:Int32, target:Float32, max_force:Float32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `constraint` | In | Int32 | required | A hinge or slider constraint. |
| `mode` | In | Int32 | required | 0 off, 1 speed, 2 position. |
| `target` | In | Float32 | required | The speed or position to reach. |
| `max_force` | In | Float32 | required | The largest torque or force the motor may use, 0 or more. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Drives a hinge or a slider. Mode 0 turns the motor off, mode 1 drives to a speed (degrees per second, world units per second), mode 2 drives to a position (degrees, world units). The motor never pushes harder than `max_force` (torque for a hinge, force for a slider), so a weak motor can be stopped by a load.

## Differences

* The original has no such command. This is an extension; programs that use it do not compile with the original Blitz3D.
